title: Lee Apologizes, Rules Out Re-Election Bid as Approval Hits Record Low 37%
detail: At a Blue House press conference, President Lee Jae-myung apologized to the public over housing policy, Cabinet appointment controversies and an ETF-related dispute, saying "I would like to begin by expressing my apologies to the people who continue to struggle through their daily lives in difficult circumstances," and vowed to be more humble. He also said he has no intention of seeking re-election. The statement came as a new Gallup Korea poll put his approval at 37% — a fourth consecutive weekly decline and a new low since his June 2025 inauguration — with disapproval up 5 points to 56%, the widest gap of his presidency. Pollsters cited accumulating discontent over housing affordability and personnel appointments plus growing economic pessimism, just five months after his approval peaked.

media.caption: President Lee Jae-myung apologizes at a Blue House press conference as his approval rating hits a record low of 37%

title: Lee Rules Out Troop Deployment to Hormuz Despite Trump Pressure
detail: President Lee Jae-myung said South Korea would not deploy troops or military assets to participate in the Middle East conflict, reiterating three times that "there will be no deployment involving participation or intervention in the war" and that the principle of non-deployment "remains unchanged." The statement came under sustained pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, who had criticized Seoul over its reluctance to help secure the Strait of Hormuz amid Washington's confrontation with Iran. Lee said Seoul was instead weighing minimal protective measures for its own commercial shipping and crude-oil imports and for the safety of Korean nationals in the region, and separately said US-North Korea talks remained possible. A recent Gallup Korea poll had found 55% of South Koreans opposed to any Hormuz deployment.

media.caption: President Lee Jae-myung says South Korea will not deploy troops to the Strait of Hormuz

title: Lee Says $350 Billion US Investment Deal Delayed Over Unresolved Terms, Causing 'Sleepless Nights'
detail: President Lee Jae-myung said South Korea and the United States are still renegotiating parts of the $350 billion strategic investment package agreed as part of the tariff deal that lowered US duties on Korean goods from roughly 25% to 15%. "I myself have spent sleepless nights thinking about this... it carries enormous weight," Lee said, adding that after discovering unacceptable terms in a nearly completed agreement for the first investment project, he ordered further discussions rather than sign off. The sticking point is a 'commercial reasonableness' clause covering how investment returns are recovered, revenue is shared and losses are allocated; Lee said Seoul would back only projects that are commercially rational, stressing that "$350 billion represents taxpayers' money." The delay pushed back Seoul's planned unveiling of its first project under the commitment and a related parliamentary briefing.

media.caption: President Lee Jae-myung says the $350 billion US investment deal remains unresolved over commercial-reasonableness terms
